anomaly_def.Name: Storage Space Capacity Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly: Free physical or logical space for data, logs, temp, or backup areas is exhausted, halting allocation and growth operations.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly: Network links, listener, socket, or session-handling resources saturate or stall, preventing timely establishment and servicing of client connections.

When both conditions manifest concurrently, the database experiences compounded symptoms: connection attempts pile up while existing sessions hang on client-read/client-write waits; DML or bulk-load operations abruptly fail with out-of-space errors that cascade into log-archive backpressure, yet the related error and retry storms further overload the listener and network queues. Monitoring may show plummeting free space metrics alongside soaring connection backlog, retransmissions, and authentication latencies. Application tiers observe unpredictable timeouts—sometimes during login, other times mid-transaction—making root-cause isolation difficult.

Causally, space exhaustion can indirectly amplify network stress: failed commits and log pushes trigger client retries and connection churn, inflating socket counts and listener workload. Conversely, network stalls slow log shipping, backup writes, and archiving, delaying space reclamation and causing filesystems or tablespaces to fill more quickly. The vicious cycle of space pressure generating retry traffic, and connectivity limits preventing cleanup or maintenance from freeing space, accelerates service degradation and risks a complete outage if neither resource constraint is relieved promptly.

entry.official_definition: Specifies the amount of time with no network activity after which the operating system should send a TCP keepalive message to the client.
entry.trigger_condition: A TCP client connection has no network activity longer than tcp_keepalives_idle on systems supporting TCP_KEEPIDLE or an equivalent socket option.
entry.workload_impact: Starts TCP keepalive probing for an otherwise idle client connection; together with interval and count settings this can lead to dead connection detection.
entry.default_behavior: Default value is 0, selecting the operating system default.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
